title: Scalar pull and push comparisons are the specified adjoint mates
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite normed field extension, put $A=\mathcal O_E$ and fix a uniformizer $\varpi$. Let $k$ have positive prime characteristic different from $\ell$, and let all schemes mentioned be separated and of finite type over $k$. Require explicitly that each scheme is Noetherian and finite dimensional and that $\ell$ is invertible in its local rings. On the small pro-etale site put $A_T=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_T$ and $E_T(V)=C(|V|,E)$, with pointwise operations; regard $E_T$ as an $A_T$-algebra through the canonical isomorphism $A_T\cong(V\mapsto C(|V|,A))$ of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] followed by postcomposition with the inclusion $A\subset E$. Use the integral category $\mathcal I_T=\Dbc(T,A)$ of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] and its raw scalar localization $\mathcal R_T=\mathcal I_T[1/\varpi]$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. Let $h:T\to U$ be any $k$-morphism, let $F_T,F_U$ be the ambient scalar extensions of [lem-weil-pbc-realization-scalar-functor], and put $P_h=Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and $Q_h=Rh_{*,A}$ on integral constructible objects. Their adjunction uses the inverse of the actual completion unit to identify $P_h$ with ordinary pullback [lem-weil-pbc-realization-completed-pull]. Put $P_h^E=Lh_c^*$ and $Q_h^E=Rh_{c,*}$ with their ambient adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. For the specified comparisons $\alpha:F_TP_h\simeq P_h^EF_U$ and $\beta:F_UQ_h\simeq Q_h^EF_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-realization-completed-pull] and [lem-weil-pbc-realization-localized-push], the direct-image comparison is the right adjoint mate of the pullback comparison. Explicitly, for integral $N$ on $U$ and $M$ on $T$,
$$Q_h^E(\alpha_N)\,\beta_{P_hN}\,F_U(\eta_N)=\eta^E_{F_UN},\qquad F_T(\epsilon_M)=\epsilon^E_{F_TM}\,P_h^E(\beta_M)\,\alpha_{Q_hM}.$$
Here $\eta,\epsilon$ and $\eta^E,\epsilon^E$ are the respective units and counits, and compositions are read right to left. These equations persist for the localized adjunctions of [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport].

proof.text: First work with ordinary ambient $P=Lh_A^*$ and $Q=Rh_{*,A}$, and write $P^E=Lh_c^*$, $Q^E=Rh_{c,*}$. The completed-pull comparison gives the actual natural isomorphism $\gamma:P\xrightarrow{\sim}P_h$ on integral objects, and identifies the integral adjunction with $P\dashv Q$ by precisely $\gamma^{-1}$. Under this identification the specified $\alpha$ becomes the ordinary scalar-pull comparison. Thus an equation proved using ordinary $P$, its unit and its counit is the required completed equation after inserting $\gamma$ and $\gamma^{-1}$; adjacent inverse factors cancel. Both $P$ and $Q$ preserve the integral constructible categories by the pull and push statements, so their ambient units and counits restrict to these full subcategories.

proof.text:
Write $r_W$ for ambient restriction of scalars and $j_W:\mathrm{id}\to r_WF_W$ for the scalar-extension unit, for $W=T,U$. The coefficient description gives $E_W=A_W[1/\varpi]$. The current completed-pull statement specifies $c_h:h^{-1}A_U\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$ as the adjunct of precomposition with $V\times_UT\to V$, and specifies the $E$-coefficient isomorphism as its localization at $\varpi$. These are the actual coefficient maps used by $P$ and $P^E$. The square with $A\to E$ commutes: under the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction its two composites are precomposition of continuous $A$-valued functions followed by the inclusion into $E$, or that inclusion followed by precomposition, which agree. The localization comparison sends $a/\varpi^n$ to the pulled numerator with the same denominator. The coefficient-change theorem therefore applies and supplies
$$b:r_TP^E\xrightarrow{\sim}Pr_U,\qquad d:r_UQ^E\xrightarrow{\sim}Qr_T,$$
with its stated compatibility of adjuncts. All functors here are ambient; in particular $r_WF_WM$ need not be integral constructible.

proof.text:
In this notation the normalizations of the two specified comparisons say
$$r_T(\alpha_N)\,j_{T,PN}=b_{F_UN}^{-1}P(j_{U,N}),\qquad
r_U(\beta_M)\,j_{U,QM}=d_{F_TM}^{-1}Q(j_{T,M}).$$
The first equation is exactly preservation of the localization unit by the scalar-pull comparison, after removing $\gamma$ as in step 1. The second is exactly the extension/restriction transpose used to define the scalar-push comparison: the map out of $QM$ is $Q(j_{T,M})$, followed by $d^{-1}$. These are equations of derived morphisms, supplied by the cited normalizations; no computation with representatives of derived sections is being assumed.

proof.text:
For any ambient $E_T$-complex $Z$, apply the coefficient-change adjunct equation to the counit $t=\epsilon^E_Z:P^EQ^EZ\to Z$, whose adjunct is $1_{Q^EZ}$. Its restricted adjunct is $d_Z$. Inverting the ordinary $P\dashv Q$ hom bijection therefore gives
$$r_T(\epsilon^E_Z)b_{Q^EZ}^{-1}=\epsilon_{r_TZ}P(d_Z).$$
This uses the counit of the ambient integral adjunction at $r_TZ$, not a counit whose domain is restricted to constructible integral objects.

proof.text:
Fix integral $M$ and transpose both sides of the desired counit equation along $F_T\dashv r_T$. The transpose of $F_T(\epsilon_M)$ is $j_{T,M}\epsilon_M$ by naturality of $j_T$. Using step 3, naturality of $b$, step 3 again, and step 4 with $Z=F_TM$, the transpose of the other side is
$$\begin{aligned}
r_T(\epsilon^E_{F_TM})\,r_TP^E(\beta_M)\,r_T(\alpha_{QM})\,j_{T,PQM}
&=r_T(\epsilon^E_{F_TM})\,b_{Q^EF_TM}^{-1}P\bigl(r_U(\beta_M)j_{U,QM}\bigr)\\
&=r_T(\epsilon^E_{F_TM})\,b_{Q^EF_TM}^{-1}P(d_{F_TM}^{-1})PQ(j_{T,M})\\
&=\epsilon_{r_TF_TM}PQ(j_{T,M})=j_{T,M}\epsilon_M.
\end{aligned}$$
The final equality is naturality of the ambient counit. Injectivity of the scalar adjunction's hom bijection proves $F_T(\epsilon_M)=\epsilon^E_{F_TM}P^E(\beta_M)\alpha_{QM}$. By the definition of a square mate this identifies $\beta$ as the mate of $\alpha^{-1}$ (the inverse is required by the direction convention in that definition), equivalently the claimed compatibility with the displayed pull isomorphism.

proof.text:
For integral $N$ put $D_N=Q^E(\alpha_N)\beta_{PN}F_U(\eta_N)$. Transpose it along $P^E\dashv Q^E$. Naturality of $\epsilon^E$, the counit equation of step 5 at $PN$, and naturality of $\alpha$ at $\eta_N$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\epsilon^E_{P^EF_UN}P^E(D_N)
&=\alpha_N\epsilon^E_{F_TPN}P^E(\beta_{PN})P^EF_U(\eta_N)\\
&=\alpha_NF_T(\epsilon_{PN})\alpha_{QPN}^{-1}P^EF_U(\eta_N)\\
&=\alpha_NF_T\bigl(\epsilon_{PN}P(\eta_N)\bigr)\alpha_N^{-1}=1.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the triangle identity of $P\dashv Q$. The transpose of $\eta^E_{F_UN}$ is also the identity by its triangle identity. Injectivity of the same hom bijection yields $D_N=\eta^E_{F_UN}$. Step 1 now restores the specified completed adjunction in both equations.

proof.text: Finally raw rationalization has the same objects and morphisms $u/\varpi^n$. Extend the integral functors, unit and counit by rational transport. Naturality on a fraction is the integral naturality equation multiplied by $\varpi^{-n}$, and the two triangle identities hold because their components are the images of the integral components. Hence these are the localized adjunctions. The realization functors send $u/\varpi^n$ to $\varpi^{-n}F_W(u)$; the same scalar calculation extends naturality of $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Every object of the raw localization is already an integral object, and the components of the two equations are exactly those proved in steps 5 and 6. Consequently both equations hold for the localized adjunctions as well. No choice of rational lattice or passage to an idempotent completion enters this argument.
